You are reverse-engineering, PURELY AS A BLACK BOX, the behavior of this program:

    /workspace/dataset/test5_executable --a '<instance JSON>' --b '<schema JSON>'

It is a PyInstaller bundle of this Python script (jsonschema 4.23.0, CPython 3.x):

    instance = json.loads(args.a); schema = json.loads(args.b)
    validator = Draft7Validator(schema)
    errors = list(validator.iter_errors(instance))
    print(len(errors))

So stdout is the NUMBER OF TOP-LEVEL ValidationErrors yielded by iter_errors, then a newline.
Nonzero exit = unhandled Python exception (stdout empty). Exit 2 = argparse usage error.

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT:
- NEVER run 'python'/'python3'. Only run the executable. Do not try to unpack or read the bundle's source.
- Your job is EMPIRICAL: form a hypothesis, then run cases to confirm/refute. Report only what you OBSERVED.
- The consumer of your report is an engineer reimplementing this in pure Node.js ESM with zero dependencies.
  What they need from you: exact error-count semantics, and every place naive JS would diverge from Python.

WORKFLOW (do all of it):
1. Author a case file /workspace/probe/cases/<FAMILY>.json — a JSON array of {"a": "<instance json string>", "b": "<schema json string>", "note": "what this pins down"}.
   Write it with the Write tool (it is plain JSON; remember a/b are STRINGS containing JSON).
2. Run: node /workspace/probe/harness.mjs /workspace/probe/cases/<FAMILY>.json
   It prints one line per case (out="N\n" or EXIT code) and saves observed results to /workspace/probe/observed/<FAMILY>.json.
   You may also invoke the executable directly for quick one-off checks.
3. Iterate: when a result surprises you, add cases to isolate the rule. Aim for 45-110 cases that are DECISIVE, not repetitive.
4. IMPORTANT: every case in your final case file must have been run through the harness so its observed output is recorded.
   The observed file is the regression corpus the implementer will test against - it must be complete and correct.

Report your findings via the structured output tool. Be dense and specific: "properties yields one error per failing
subschema, and nested errors propagate individually (instance {"a":{"b":1}} vs properties.a.properties.b.type=string
plus a.required=[z,y] => 3)" is useful; "properties works as expected" is useless.

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC for family "ref-resolution". Another agent already probed it and wrote
/workspace/probe/cases/ref-resolution.json (observed results in /workspace/probe/observed/ref-resolution.json).

Their report:
RULES:
- Resolution uses the MODERN `referencing` engine (NOT legacy RefResolver): failures are _WrappedReferencingError wrapping PointerToNowhere / Unresolvable / NoSuchAnchor / InvalidAnchor. Every resolution failure is an EXCEPTION (exit 1, empty stdout), never a validation error.
- $ref SIBLINGS ARE ALWAYS DROPPED. b={"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"boolean"}: a=1 => 1 (NOT 2); a="s" => 0 (proves the sibling was dropped, since type:boolean would fail). Only $ref, $schema and $id matter in a $ref-bearing object.
- Sibling dropping is DIALECT-INDEPENDENT — it still happens when the subschema declares $schema 2019-09 or 2020-12: {"definitions":{"x":true},"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"string","maximum":0}]} vs 1 => 0. Key order irrelevant ($ref last => still 0).
- Control proving it is $ref-specific, not a broken 2020-12 dialect: {"allOf":[{"$schema":"...2020-12/schema","maximum":0,"type":"string"}]} vs 1 => 2.
- $ref yields the target's errors INDIVIDUALLY, flattened, with no wrapper error. definitions.x={"required":["a"],"minProperties":2}: {"$ref":"#/definitions/x"} vs {} => 2; that target under items with [{},{}] => 4; reached via ref->ref chain => 2; under additionalProperties with {"a":1,"b":2} => 2; anyOf inside the target still collapses to 1.
- Counts compose additively: {"definitions":{"x":{"required":["b"],"minProperties":1}},"properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}},"required":["z"]} vs {"a":{}} => 3. Same $ref twice in allOf => 2.
- $ref works inside items, properties, additionalProperties, allOf, not, if/then, dependencies, propertyNames. $ref to true => 0, to false => 1, to {} => 0.
- Local pointers resolve against the ROOT document (the whole --b value) from any depth, unless an intervening $id changed the base.
- Pointer resolution is a generic JSON-Pointer walk: into arrays (#/allOf/0 => 1, #/allOf/1 => 0 for allOf:[{type:string},{type:integer}] vs 1), into arrays under UNKNOWN keywords (#/x/0), into nested definitions (#/definitions/x/definitions/y), and to non-schema containers (#/definitions returns the definitions map, validated as a schema of all-unknown keys => 0).
- A pointer target that is not an object or a boolean => EXCEPTION: string => AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get'; int => TypeError argument of type 'int' is not iterable; null => TypeError NoneType; array => AttributeError 'list' has no attribute 'get'. Holds at every position (#/type, #/required, #/definitions/x, unknown keys).
- Walking THROUGH a segment whose value is an array also throws before later segments apply: {"definitions":{"x":[{...},{...}]},"$ref":"#/definitions/x/1"} => AttributeError 'list' (the /1 never runs).
- Pointer escapes use RFC 6901 order (~1 -> '/' first, then ~0 -> '~'): key 'a/b' via #/definitions/a~1b => 1; 'a~b' via a~0b => 1; with BOTH 'a~1b' and 'a/b' present, a~01b resolves to 'a~1b' => 1.
- The fragment is PERCENT-DECODED ONCE over the WHOLE fragment BEFORE splitting on '/': %20 finds key 'a b' => 1; %25 -> '%'; %7E0 -> '~0' -> '~' (percent decode precedes ~-unescaping); %2520 finds the literal key 'a%20b' => 1; %2F becomes a real separator, so #/definitions/a%2Fb does NOT find key 'a/b' (PointerToNowhere) but DOES address definitions/a/b => 1.
- A raw space is legal in $ref and matches key 'a b' => 1. '+' is NOT decoded to space (matches only a literal 'a+b' key). Trailing whitespace in a pointer is significant.
- Array indices are parsed with Python int(): '-1' = LAST element (allOf:[{type:string},{type:integer}] vs 1 => 0), '-2' = first (=> 1); '00' => 0; '+1', ' 1\t' (%201%09) and the FULLWIDTH digit '１' all => index 1; '1_0' => 10; '1.0' and 'x' => ValueError exception; out-of-range (5, -3, or 1_0 with 2 elements) => PointerToNowhere exception.
- Python strings are Sequences, so a numeric segment indexes INTO a string value: {"x":"abc"} with #/x/9 => PointerToNowhere, #/x/z => ValueError, #/x/1 => resolves to "b" then throws AttributeError as a non-schema target.
- Missing target => PointerToNowhere (#/definitions/nope, #/a/b/c, #//definitions/x whose empty first segment misses). $ref with no leading '#' ('/definitions/x', 'other.json', ' ') => Unresolvable, and NO network fetch is attempted. Non-string $ref => AttributeError 'int' has no attribute 'startswith'.
- A fragment that is neither empty, nor '/'-prefixed, nor a registered plain-name anchor => InvalidAnchor exception ('#definitions/x').
- Refs that re-enter without consuming instance => RecursionError exception: {"$ref":"#"}, {"$ref":""}, {"allOf":[{"$ref":"#"}]}, mutual definitions a->b->a, {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","allOf":[{"$ref":"http://ex.com/a"}]}.
- Recursion that consumes instance is fine: self-recursive definition over a linked list => 0; mutual a->b->a with {"next":{"next":{}}} where b has required:[z] => 1; {"properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}},"required":["a"]} vs {"a":{}} => 1; a depth-40 chain => 0.
- Root $id registers the root document under that URI so absolute self-refs work: {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x"}]} => 1.
- DRAFT-7 LEGACY id_of: $id is IGNORED whenever the SAME object also has a $ref, and when it is fragment-only ('#anch'). So {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x","definitions":{...}} => Unresolvable (root never registered under that URI) while the same with $ref:"#/definitions/x" => 1; and {"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]} resolves against the ROOT => 1, whereas {"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]}]} => PointerToNowhere because there the base URI did change.
- Subschema $id registers a subresource: absolute ('http://ex.com/sub' => 1), relative resolved against the parent base ('sub.json' under root $id http://ex.com/root => 1), and dot-segment ('./sub' under http://ex.com/d/root => 1). A new base plus its own definitions shadows the root's: {"$id":"foo.json","definitions":{"x":{"type":"integer"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]} => 0. urn: bases work.
- URIs are NOT case-normalized: $ref 'HTTP://EX.COM/sub' against $id 'http://ex.com/sub' => Unresolvable exception.
- Draft-4-style "id" is never honored, even inside a subschema declaring $schema draft-04: root {"id":"http://ex.com/a"} + $ref to that URI => Unresolvable exception.
- Plain-name anchors: draft7 declares them via $id:"#xa" ({"definitions":{"x":{"$id":"#xa","type":"string"}},"$ref":"#xa"} => 1). $anchor is NOT a draft7 keyword => NoSuchAnchor exception, but it works once that subschema sets $schema 2020-12 => 1.
- ROOT $schema IS IGNORED (Draft7Validator is constructed explicitly): {"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","const":5} vs 1 => 1 (draft7 const still applies).
- $schema in ANY SUBSCHEMA DOES switch the dialect for that subschema and everything below: draft-04 subschema ignores const ({"properties":{"p":{"$schema":draft4,"const":5}}} vs {"p":1} => 0) and uses boolean exclusiveMaximum ({"$schema":draft4,"maximum":5,"exclusiveMaximum":true} vs {"p":3} => 0 while the same without $schema => 1); 2019-09 subschema honors dependentRequired ({"a":1} => 1 vs 0 for draft7); 2020-12 subschema honors prefixItems ({"a":[1]} => 1 vs 0).
- The switched dialect propagates DOWN into nested subschemas AND THROUGH $ref into the resolved target: {"allOf":[{"$schema":"...2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/definitions/x"}],"definitions":{"x":{"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]}}} vs [1] => 1; control without $schema => 0.
- An UNRECOGNIZED $schema silently falls back to the CURRENTLY ACTIVE dialect (not draft7, not latest): 'bogus://x' nested inside a 2020-12 subschema still honors prefixItems => 1; 'http://json-schema.org/schema#' (latest alias) and draft-03 at draft7 level keep draft7 (dependentRequired ignored, only maximum fires => 1).
- A non-string $schema => AttributeError 'int' object has no attribute 'decode' (exception).
- Meta-schemas are BUNDLED offline: {"$ref":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"} vs 1 => 1 (fails the meta-schema's type:[object,boolean]); vs {"type":123} => 1; draft-04 meta => 1; {"allOf":[{"$ref":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"}]} vs 1 => 8 (its own type check + the 7 vocabulary subschemas it $refs). Any OTHER remote/relative URI => Unresolvable exception.
- definitions/$defs subschemas are never evaluated unless referenced: {"definitions":{"bad":{"type":"nonsense"}},"type":"integer"} vs 1 => 0; {"definitions":{"bad":{"$ref":"#/nope"}},"type":"integer"} => 0. Referencing the broken one raises jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType.
GOTCHAS:
- Array-index segments go through Python int(), which accepts far more than /^\d+$/. NEGATIVE INDICES WRAP: b={"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/-1"} a=1 => 0 (last element), "#/allOf/-2" => 1 (first element). Naive JS arr["-1"] is undefined -> you would report not-found.
- int() also accepts leading zeros ('#/allOf/00' => index 0 => 1), a leading plus ('#/allOf/%2B1' => index 1 => 0), surrounding ASCII whitespace ('#/allOf/%201%09' => index 1 => 0), UNICODE DIGITS ('#/allOf/１' with U+FF11 => index 1 => 0) and UNDERSCORE SEPARATORS ('#/allOf/1_0' == 10, so with 11 elements => 0 and with 2 elements => PointerToNowhere). But it rejects '1.0' and 'x' with a ValueError EXCEPTION (exit 1), which is a DIFFERENT outcome from the not-found PointerToNowhere exception.
- Percent-decoding is applied ONCE to the ENTIRE fragment BEFORE splitting on '/', so %2F creates a new segment: b={"definitions":{"a/b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%2Fb"} => EXCEPTION (PointerToNowhere), while b={"definitions":{"a":{"b":{"type":"string"}}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%2Fb"} => 1. JS code that splits first and decodeURIComponent()s each segment gets both cases backwards.
- Python's urllib unquote LEAVES MALFORMED ESCAPES ALONE; JS decodeURIComponent THROWS URIError. b={"definitions":{"a%zzb":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%zzb"} => 1 (resolves). A JS port must implement a tolerant %XX decoder (and it must be UTF-8 aware: '#/definitions/%C3%A9' finds key 'é' => 1).
- unquote does NOT treat '+' as a space (unlike form decoding, and unlike some JS URL helpers). b={"definitions":{"a b":{...}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a+b"} => EXCEPTION, while b={"definitions":{"a+b":{...}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a+b"} => 1.
- ~-unescaping happens AFTER percent-decoding and only in the RFC 6901 order (~1 then ~0): b={"definitions":{"a~b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%7E0b"} => 1 (%7E -> '~', giving '~0', which then becomes '~'). And with both keys present, b={"definitions":{"a~1b":{"type":"string"},"a/b":{"type":"integer"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a~01b"} a=1 => 1, i.e. it picks 'a~1b', not 'a/b'.
- Python strings are indexable Sequences, so a pointer can walk INTO a string value. b={"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/9"} => PointerToNowhere; b={"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/z"} => ValueError; b={"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/1"} => AttributeError (resolved to the character "b", then used as a schema). A JS port indexing only objects/arrays would call all three 'not found'.
- Truthiness/type of the pointer TARGET decides the exception flavor, and none of them are validation errors: string target -> AttributeError, int -> TypeError 'not iterable', null -> TypeError NoneType, array -> AttributeError. So a JS port must EXIT NONZERO (not emit a count) for b={"definitions":{"x":5},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}.
- Draft-7's legacy id_of returns None when the object ALSO has a $ref, so $id is silently discarded there. b={"$id":"http://ex.com/a","$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}}} a=1 => EXCEPTION (Unresolvable) even though the URI textually equals the root $id; removing the root $ref (putting it under allOf) makes the same URI resolve => 1.
- Correspondingly, a subschema $id is ignored when it sits next to $ref: {"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]} => 1 (root-relative), but nesting the ref one level deeper, {"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]}]} => EXCEPTION. Same $id, opposite outcome.
- $ref siblings are dropped even when the subschema opts into 2019-09/2020-12 via $schema — the opposite of what those specs say and of what most JS validators (ajv) do. {"definitions":{"x":true},"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"string","maximum":0}]} a=1 => 0. Do NOT special-case 2019/2020 to apply siblings.
- The ROOT $schema is ignored but a SUBSCHEMA $schema is honored — the reverse of the usual assumption. a=1 b={"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","const":5} => 1 (draft7 const runs), yet a={"p":1} b={"properties":{"p":{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","const":5}}} => 0. A JS port must implement per-subschema dialect switching (draft4/6/7/2019-09/2020-12 keyword tables) and must inherit the active dialect for unknown $schema values.
- Meta-schemas resolve OFFLINE from a bundled registry, so remote refs are not uniformly fatal. a=1 b={"allOf":[{"$ref":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"}]} => 8 (not an error, not 1); b={"$ref":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"} => 1; but b={"$ref":"other.json"} => EXCEPTION. Hard-coding 'any absolute URI throws' is wrong.
- Unbounded ref recursion becomes a CPython RecursionError (exit 1), not a hang and not a cycle-detection error: b={"$ref":"#"} and b={"$ref":""} both exit 1. There is also a DEPTH LIMIT on legitimate recursion: for schema {"definitions":{"n":{"properties":{"next":{"$ref":"#/definitions/n"}}}},"$ref":"#/definitions/n"} a linked list of depth 246 => 0 but depth 248 => exit 1 (RecursionError); the boundary drops to ~200 when an anyOf is added per level, so it is frame-count dependent, not a fixed schema depth.
- "$ref":"" (empty string) and "$ref":"#" behave identically (both resolve to the root), whereas "$ref":"/definitions/x" (no '#') is Unresolvable and "$ref":"#definitions/x" is InvalidAnchor. Three different failure paths for three near-identical strings.
- URI comparison is byte-exact: 'HTTP://EX.COM/sub' does not match $id 'http://ex.com/sub' => Unresolvable. JS code using `new URL()` normalizes scheme and host to lowercase and would resolve it.
EXCEPTIONS:
- --a 1 --b {"$ref":"#/definitions/nope"}   (PointerToNowhere)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#//definitions/x"}   (PointerToNowhere, empty segment)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"/definitions/x"}   (Unresolvable, no '#')
- --a 1 --b {"$ref":5}   (AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'startswith')
- --a 1 --b {"$ref":"#definitions/x","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}}}   (InvalidAnchor)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"a b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a+b"}   (PointerToNowhere: '+' is not a space)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"a%20b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%20b"}   (PointerToNowhere: %20 decoded to a space)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"a/b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%2Fb"}   (PointerToNowhere: %2F became a separator)
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/5"}   (PointerToNowhere, index out of range)
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/-3"}   (PointerToNowhere, negative index out of range)
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/1_0"}   (PointerToNowhere: int('1_0')==10)
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/x"}   (ValueError: invalid literal for int())
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/1.0"}   (ValueError: invalid literal for int())
- --a 1 --b {"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/9"}   (PointerToNowhere, string index out of range)
- --a 1 --b {"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/z"}   (ValueError: invalid literal for int())
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":"hello"},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}   (AttributeError: 'str' has no attribute 'get')
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":5},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}   (TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":null},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}   (TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}]},"$ref":"#/definitions/x/1"}   (AttributeError: 'list' has no attribute 'get')
- --a 1 --b {"type":"integer","$ref":"#/type"}   (AttributeError: 'str' has no attribute 'get')
- --a 1 --b {"$ref":"#"}   (RecursionError)
- --a 1 --b {"$ref":""}   (RecursionError)
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"$ref":"#"}]}   (RecursionError)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"a":{"$ref":"#/definitions/b"},"b":{"$ref":"#/definitions/a"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a"}   (RecursionError)
- --a 1 --b {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","allOf":[{"$ref":"http://ex.com/a"}]}   (RecursionError)
- --a 1 --b {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}}}   (Unresolvable: root $id suppressed by the $ref sibling)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]}]}   (PointerToNowhere: base URI changed)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"s":{"$id":"http://ex.com/sub","type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"HTTP://EX.COM/sub"}]}   (Unresolvable: no case normalization)
- --a 1 --b {"id":"http://ex.com/a","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x"}]}   (Unresolvable: draft4 'id' not honored)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":{"$anchor":"xa","type":"string"}},"$ref":"#xa"}   (NoSuchAnchor: $anchor is not a draft7 keyword)
- --a 1 --b {"allOf":[{"$schema":5,"maximum":0}]}   (AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'decode')
- --a 1 --b {"$ref":"other.json"}   (Unresolvable, no network fetch)
- --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"bad":{"type":"nonsense"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/bad"}   (jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType)
- NOT in the corpus but observed: a linked list of depth 248 against {"definitions":{"n":{"properties":{"next":{"$ref":"#/definitions/n"}}}},"$ref":"#/definitions/n"} exits 1 with RecursionError (depth 246 => 0).

Original focus list for this family:
$ref under Draft7 (jsonschema 4.23 legacy RefResolver).
- SIBLING KEYWORDS: {"$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"boolean",...} — are siblings ignored entirely? Prove with a case
  where sibling and target disagree, and where BOTH would fail (count 1 vs 2).
- Local JSON pointers: "#", "#/definitions/x", "#/properties/a", pointer INTO an array "#/allOf/0", pointer with
  escaping "~0"/"~1" (keys "a/b" and "a~b"), percent-encoded "%25"/"%20"/"%7E" in pointers, empty fragment "#",
  pointer to a boolean schema, pointer to a non-schema value (e.g. to a string or number => exception?).
- Missing pointer target => exception? Malformed ref "#/a/b/c" ; ref to itself "#" (infinite recursion => exception?);
  mutually recursive refs via definitions (a->b->a) with an instance that terminates the recursion (e.g. linked list) — does it work?
- $id / $anchor: does a subschema "$id" change the base URI (does {"$id":"foo","$ref":"#/x"} still resolve locally)?
  Root "$id":"http://x/y" plus "$ref":"#/definitions/z"; "$ref":"other.json" (network => exception?);
  "$ref":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" (network attempt => exception? or bundled?).
- Does a nested "$schema" (e.g. draft-04 or draft-06 inside a subschema/definition) change the dialect used for that
  subschema? Design a DECISIVE test: draft4 exclusiveMaximum:true+maximum, or draft4 "id" vs "$id", or draft6 "contains"
  in a draft4 subschema, or "dependentRequired" (draft2019) inside a subschema with $schema 2019-09.
- $ref to a definition that itself has a $ref; $ref inside items/properties/allOf; count multiplicity through refs.
- "definitions" itself is never validated (a broken schema under definitions that is never referenced => 0 errors)?

YOUR JOB — be adversarial, assume their report is incomplete or wrong:
1. Read their case file. Find what the focus list asked for that they did NOT actually test, and any rule they stated
   that their cases do not actually prove (over-generalization). Numeric/precision/unicode/exception boundaries are the
   usual blind spots.
2. Independently RE-VERIFY their 5 most surprising or load-bearing claims by running the executable yourself. If a
   claim is wrong, say so loudly in your rules with the disproving case.
3. Author /workspace/probe/cases/ref-resolution-x.json with 30-80 NEW decisive cases covering the gaps and the boundaries
   (especially: off-by-one boundaries, type-skipping, the exception/no-exception frontier, and anything where a naive
   JS port would silently differ). Run it through the harness: node /workspace/probe/harness.mjs /workspace/probe/cases/ref-resolution-x.json
4. Report the MERGED, corrected rule set for this family (yours + theirs, corrections applied), with corpusPath
   "/workspace/probe/observed/ref-resolution.json,/workspace/probe/observed/ref-resolution-x.json" and caseCount = total cases across both.
Your rules list is the specification the implementer will code against. Make it complete, ordered, and unambiguous.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
